name: Is metal roofing a more expensive option than asphalt shingles?

mainEntity.name: Is metal roofing a more expensive option than asphalt shingles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Generally, the upfront cost of metal roofing is higher than traditional asphalt shingles. However, the long-term cost-effectiveness often makes it a worthwhile investment. Metal roofs typically last 40-70 years, significantly longer than asphalt, which usually needs replacement every 15-30 years. When comparing options, consider the total cost of ownership, including potential energy savings and reduced maintenance, which can offset the initial expenditure over decades.
acceptedAnswer.description: Metal roofing typically has a higher upfront cost than asphalt shingles, but it offers long-term savings due to its extended lifespan and durability.
